reason: The passage portrays Yahweh as actively supportive of the Hebrew people through David's kingship. Key evidence includes: (1) Yahweh explicitly commissions David to 'shepherd My people Israel' (וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְךָ אַתָּה תִרְעֶה אֶת־ עַמִּי); (2) Yahweh grants military victories—'Yahweh saved with a great salvation' (וַיּוֹשַׁע יְהוָה תְּשׁוּעָה גְדוֹלָה); (3) Yahweh's continuous presence is emphasized—'Yahweh of hosts was with him' (וַיהוָה צְבָאוֹת עִמּוֹ); (4) The anointing of David as king occurs 'according to the word of Yahweh' (כִּדְבַר יְהוָה). The passage consistently demonstrates divine favor and support for Israel, not antagonism.
